messages:
mara_sales: Heads-up - Client Infra (AcmeHealth2) asked for Private POC. They say PrivateLink preferred by security but infra ops favors VPC Peering. Need clear ops instructions.
oliver_solns: Both supported. PL = simpler (no route edits), good for cross-account. Peering = direct, lower hop count but adds route+SG work. Ask which they want.
nina_net: For peering we need: client account id, client VPC id, their subnet ids + route table ids, and verify CIDR no-overlap. If they use a firewall VPC, give that VPC id too.
tom_sre: Security requirements: TLS enforced, KMS CMK for logs, and audit log push to their S3 if requested. For PrivateLink we will provide a service name and SG recommendation (allow outbound 443 to our service).
poc_bot: POC policy: temporary API key valid 10 days, quota checks applied. Create JIRA if token quota exceeded.
client_infra: Ops: we prefer peering because of inline firewall. Our VPCs: app 10.40.0.0/16, infra/firewall 10.10.0.0/16. We'll share route table ids.
oliver_solns: Sample peering steps to hand to them: 1) create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-client --peer-vpc-id vpc-redwood --peer-owner-id 987654321000 2) accept peering 3) add routes in both route tables to point at pcx-xxxxxx 4) update SGs to allow 443 from peer CIDR.
nina_net: Sample Terraform for interface endpoint (if they change mind): resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "ri" { vpc_id = var.vpc_id service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-zzzz" vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface" subnet_ids = var.subnets private_dns_enabled = true }
tom_sre: Ask client whether outbound to metrics/control plane (metrics.redwood.ai:443) is allowed. If not, we can disable metrics for POC. Also request a technical contact for the ops call.
mara_sales: I'll send a consolidated checklist and the two snippets to the client and schedule a 30-min ops call with oliver and nina. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
